narrative: Fire leads today's brief: a new synthesis dataset pools post-fire biodiversity data from Australia's 2019–2020 megafires, a global review argues the fire crisis reflects compounding human and bioclimatic drivers, and fire mosaics are shown to shape connectivity and genetic diversity in two Australian bat species. Animal movement and behaviour are strongly represented, with GPS data from 586 individuals of 23 mammal species during lockdowns showing that human presence rather than buildings drives avoidance, female bears balancing human food subsidies against risk, and continent-wide tracking confirming European wildcats rely on landscape mosaics. On climate, mountain mammals and birds shifting upslope increasingly encounter unfavourable land use, while dormice torpor patterns are linked to climate conditions. A century-long Austrian resurvey attributes up to 50% local plant diversity loss to combined local and global drivers, and global mapping of cultivated plants highlights a growing pool of potential invaders. Methods are a busy area, with new open tools for bioacoustics (Bacpipe, pamflow), camera trap analysis in R (ct), and zero-shot vegetation cover estimation from plot photos (FloraScanner).
